Jenitar Na’amoana’s already had four children when she learned of surprise pregnancy ‘unheard of’ in Australia Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast A 34-year-old woman from Brisbane has defied the odds and delivered four naturally conceived, identical quadruplets in what is believed to be an Australian first. Jenitar Na’amoana, who already had four children, was not planning having another but the quadruplets emerged from a “one in 15 million” pregnancy, splitting into four from a single fertilised egg. Na’amoana duly became a mother of eight after delivering her girls by C-section at just over 28 weeks at the Royal Brisbane and Women’s hospital surrounded by a huge support team.

A mum has given birth to "unheard of" identical quadruplets in Australia. Jenitar and dad Jortham Na-amoana welcomed four baby girls, Emily, Harriet, Alexa and Catherine, at the Royal Brisbane and Women’s Hospital. They were naturally conceived and monozygotic quadruplets - where a single fertilised egg splits into four embryos. The four girls were delivered via caesarean section at 28 weeks and four days on 14 July with the chances of naturally conceiving quadruplets estimated to be around one in 15 million. The couple have now doubled their number of offspring, as they already had four children aged between 10 and one. Dr Alexa Bendall, after whom one of the babies was named, helped care for Mrs Na-amoana during her pregnancy.

"Jenitar has taken everything in her stride from day one – we have never seen a spontaneously conceived pregnancy of this type with quads, and she has somehow dodged every complication and risk for both herself and her babies to be here today, with four gorgeous newborn girls," she said. “Monozygotic quadruplets are estimated at one in every 15 million pregnancies, but to share the same placenta, this is unheard of.” The hospital said that Jenitar and Jortham were taken by "immense surprise" when told to expect quadruplets, reported news.com.au. And Dr Bendall, who is a maternal foetal medicine specialist and obstetrician, had warned that having monozygotic quadruplets is very high risk with the hospital admitting Na'amoana as a patient at 25 weeks so she could be monitored.

Jenitar Na’amoana’s already had four children when she learned of surprise pregnancy ‘unheard of’ in Australia

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A 34-year-old woman from Brisbane has defied the odds and delivered four naturally conceived, identical quadruplets in what is believed to be an Australian first.

Jenitar Na’amoana, who already had four children, was not planning having another but the quadruplets emerged from a “one in 15 million” pregnancy, splitting into four from a single fertilised egg.

Na’amoana duly became a mother of eight after delivering her girls by C-section at just over 28 weeks at the Royal Brisbane and Women’s hospital surrounded by a huge support team.

“This is unheard of ... we don’t think it has ever happened in Australia,” Alexa Bendall, a maternal foetal medicine specialist and obstetrician at the hospital, said.

“There may have been a couple of cases elsewhere in the world and when I say a couple, literally two.”

Na’amoana was still breastfeeding the youngest of her four children when she was told she had again fallen pregnant.

They got the surprise of their lives when told their “little miracle” would be a medical marvel.

“When they went along and found out they had four babies instead of one they were quite shocked,” Bendall said.

There are now four more childre in the Na’amoana household after the 14 July arrival of Emily, Harriet, Catherine and Alexa – the latter named after Dr Bendall.

The obstetrician has been caring for Na’amoana since she first discovered the surprise news of her bundles of joy.

“They are very special. We are very excited to be able to care for this amazing little family, well big family now,” Bendall said.

“One is named after me which is such a beautiful tribute.”

The pregnancy was considered very high risk but Ms Na’amoana had “taken everything in her stride from day one”, Bendall said.

“We have never seen a spontaneously conceived pregnancy of this type with quads, and she has somehow dodged every complication and risk for both herself and her babies to be here today, with four gorgeous newborn girls.”

The girls are expected to spend an extended period in the hospital before being allowed home but their long-term outlook looks really good, Bendall said.

The family have set up a GoFundMe fundraiser to help care for the girls with money going towards medical, travel and everyday living expenses as well as a van “with at least 10 or 12 seats”.

payload.title: Brisbanelaisnainen synnytti identtiset neloset – raskaus yksi 15 miljoonasta
payload.summary: Brisbanessa syntyi neljä identtistä tyttöä yhdestä hedelmöittyneestä munasolusta. Erittäin harvinainen raskaus alkoi luonnollisesti, ja kaikki sikiöt jakoivat saman istukan.
payload.content:
Brisbanelainen 34-vuotias Jenitar Na’amoana on synnyttänyt Australiassa neljä luonnollisesti alkunsa saanutta identtistä tyttöä. Yhdestä hedelmöittyneestä munasolusta kehittynyt nelosraskaus on arvioiden mukaan vain noin yksi tapaus 15 miljoonasta, ja sitä pidetään mahdollisesti ensimmäisenä laatuaan Australiassa.

## Harvinainen yhden munasolun raskaus

Emily, Harriet, Alexa ja Catherine syntyivät Royal Brisbane and Women’s Hospital -sairaalassa keisarileikkauksella 14. heinäkuuta. Raskaus oli edennyt tuolloin 28 viikkoon ja neljään päivään. Synnytyksessä oli mukana suuri hoitotiimi.

Tytöt ovat monotsygoottisia nelosia, mikä tarkoittaa, että yksi hedelmöittynyt munasolu jakautui neljäksi alkioksi. Raskaus oli alkanut spontaanisti. Arvio yhdestä tapauksesta 15 miljoonaa raskautta kohden koskee juuri tällaisia identtisiä nelosia.

Kaikki neljä sikiötä jakoivat lisäksi saman istukan. Na’amoanan hoitoon osallistunut äitiys- ja sikiölääketieteen erikoislääkäri sekä synnytyslääkäri Alexa Bendall kuvaili tätä ennenkuulumattomaksi. Hänen mukaansa hoitotiimi ei ollut aiemmin nähnyt vastaavaa luonnollisesti alkanutta nelosraskautta.

## Tiivis seuranta ennen synnytystä

Bendallin mukaan monotsygoottinen nelosraskaus oli erittäin suuren riskin raskaus. Na’amoana otettiin sairaalaan 25. raskausviikolla tarkkailua varten, jotta hänen ja vauvojen tilaa voitiin seurata ennen synnytystä.

Lääkäri sanoi Na’amoanan suhtautuneen tilanteeseen rauhallisesti alusta lähtien. Bendallin mukaan äiti ja kaikki neljä vauvaa välttyivät raskauteen liittyneiltä komplikaatioilta. Yksi tytöistä sai nimekseen Alexa raskautta hoitaneen Bendallin mukaan.

## Perheen lapsiluku kaksinkertaistui

Jenitarilla ja Jorthamilla oli ennen nelosten syntymää neljä lasta, jotka ovat iältään yhdestä kymmeneen vuotta. Jenitar ei ollut suunnitellut uutta lasta, joten tieto neljästä odotettavasta vauvasta tuli vanhemmille sairaalan mukaan valtavana yllätyksenä.

Neljän tytön syntymä kaksinkertaisti perheen lapsiluvun neljästä kahdeksaan. Sairaalan mukaan tapaus on poikkeuksellinen sekä alkunsa että sikiöiden yhteisen istukan vuoksi. Australian ensimmäistä vastaavaa tapausta koskeva arvio ei kuitenkaan ole lähdetiedoissa lopullisesti vahvistettu.

Jenitarilla ja Jorthamilla oli ennen nelosten syntymää neljä lasta, jotka ovat iältään yhdestä kymmeneen vuotta. Jenitar ei ollut suunnitellut uutta lasta, joten tieto neljästä odotettavasta vauvasta tuli vanhemmille sairaalan mukaan valtavana yllätyksenä.

Neljän tytön syntymä kaksinkertaisti perheen lapsiluvun neljästä kahdeksaan. Sairaalan mukaan tapaus on poikkeuksellinen sekä alkunsa että sikiöiden yhteisen istukan vuoksi. Australian ensimmäistä vastaavaa tapausta koskeva arvio ei kuitenkaan ole lähdetiedoissa lopullisesti vahvistettu.

Jenitar Na’amoana’s already had four children when she learned of surprise pregnancy ‘unheard of’ in Australia Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast A 34-year-old woman from Brisbane has defied the odds and delivered four naturally conceived, identical quadruplets in what is believed to be an Australian first. Jenitar Na’amoana, who already had four children, was not planning having another but the quadruplets emerged from a “one in 15 million” pregnancy, splitting into four from a single fertilised egg. Na’amoana duly became a mother of eight after delivering her girls by C-section at just over 28 weeks at the Royal Brisbane and Women’s hospital surrounded by a huge support team.

A mum has given birth to "unheard of" identical quadruplets in Australia. Jenitar and dad Jortham Na-amoana welcomed four baby girls, Emily, Harriet, Alexa and Catherine, at the Royal Brisbane and Women’s Hospital. They were naturally conceived and monozygotic quadruplets - where a single fertilised egg splits into four embryos. The four girls were delivered via caesarean section at 28 weeks and four days on 14 July with the chances of naturally conceiving quadruplets estimated to be around one in 15 million. The couple have now doubled their number of offspring, as they already had four children aged between 10 and one. Dr Alexa Bendall, after whom one of the babies was named, helped care for Mrs Na-amoana during her pregnancy.

"Jenitar has taken everything in her stride from day one – we have never seen a spontaneously conceived pregnancy of this type with quads, and she has somehow dodged every complication and risk for both herself and her babies to be here today, with four gorgeous newborn girls," she said. “Monozygotic quadruplets are estimated at one in every 15 million pregnancies, but to share the same placenta, this is unheard of.” The hospital said that Jenitar and Jortham were taken by "immense surprise" when told to expect quadruplets, reported news.com.au. And Dr Bendall, who is a maternal foetal medicine specialist and obstetrician, had warned that having monozygotic quadruplets is very high risk with the hospital admitting Na'amoana as a patient at 25 weeks so she could be monitored.
